title: Moving to Chicago and electric guitar
summary: After the season ends in St. Louis he visits a friend in Chicago, settles in 1938, marries, and gets work as an electric guitarist.

story.theme_name: Chicago: the jazz migration and its clubs
story.community_name: Going north: working the Chicago jazz scene

blocks.x: His name was Joe Bradford, a friend of mine, so I wrote a term, he told me, yes, come on up, see, so he was married and he had two daughters, and one of the girls was born while I was staying with him, so he made it so pleasant and so nice for me, like, saying I didn't have to pay a whole lot of money, and then he gave me a time to get around and make connection, you see, so well, it took me about nine months before I could actually find Wake, you know, So I finally found Wake, well, I stayed with him until about, uh, oh, I think about 40 or 41 or 43, anyhow, it was during the war, I remember, and, uh, I got married up there, and, uh, like I said, that was the time I had put down, uh, playing with the band because there wasn't so much work, I started playing with a small combination, like three, four pieces, you know. What year was that? That was around, uh, well, I say I, I, uh, I would have left the boat in 38, and I got in Chicago around September 1938, yeah, and I actually didn't start working until around, around about, uh, around about 39, see, and, uh, I had, uh, there was a couple of, uh, two places, one fellow was, uh, at Booker in Asia, one was on State Street, and one was on, uh, South Park, so you could go around there, and the guys, if they had something on the weekend, well, they, you know, they'd hire, you see. And about me playing electric and having electric guitar, well, I got quite a few jobs like that because there wasn't too many fellows with electric guitars around, around Chicago.
